name: @respawn-pi/rollover
description: The Pi extension and manual rollover skill bundled by respawn-pi.

respawnPi.note: pi-native-package-001 + pi-native-relocate-001 + pi-native-aggregate-001 (B22, B23, R1): the 21 .ts extensions under extensions/ are listed explicitly (Pi's readPiManifest requires an array of strings; convention-dir fallback applies only when the field is absent). The mcp-bridge index is enumerated alongside its peers so Pi's loader resolves and jiti-imports it as a first-class extension rather than relying on a transitive runtime import (the previous claim of transitive import was false; mcp-bridge was silently skipped on clean checkouts). The 17 source skills + 4 ops skills + 7 ops/mcp bases + 1 memory skill seed are listed explicitly so Pi discovers them without relying on fallback. skills: skills/build, checkup, comply, debug, loadout, onboard, playtest, respawn, respawn-rollover, review, run-goal, savepoint, secure, ship, skill-guard, walkthrough, wordsmith (17); ops: db-ops, deploy-verify, infra-status, secrets-audit (4); ops/mcp: context7, fly, github, graphify, runtime, security-audit, supabase (7); memory: knowledge (1). Total 29 skill surfaces. The 32-role agent bench lives alongside under agents/ but is not enumerated in pi.skills (Pi has no agent resource type; agents/*.md are surfaced via a runtime extension rather than as Pi resources).
respawnPi.bridge: The standalone root package includes adapters/pi/bridge and core; the extension resolves the bridge relative to its own installed source path.
respawnPi.security: Pi has no built-in sandbox. Use the Debian VM and a non-root account as the execution boundary.
